questionText: What is the difference between Spring Framework and Spring Boot?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can distinguish Framework programming features from Boot application assembly and identify which project owns a behavior.
outOfScope: Treating Boot and Framework as competitors

claims.statement: Spring Boot builds an application on Spring Framework and adds startup, managed dependency, and conditional configuration support rather than replacing Framework APIs.
With the servlet web starter and matching conditions, Boot supplies common MVC configuration and embedded Tomcat while the controller annotations remain Spring MVC APIs.

examples.title: Explicit MVC configuration compared with a Boot launcher and controller

validation.expected: The examples distinguish abbreviated explicit setup from the conditional Boot web path

visuals.title: Programming foundation compared with application setup

notes: Framework ownership wording was also checked against the official Spring Framework reference; its registry scope does not currently include spring-boot-intro.
The pending speakable_v2 block remains non-approved and is not the learner-facing source used by this review.

review.notes: Claims and examples were reviewed for the pinned Boot 3.3.1 and Spring-managed baseline. Final visual and editorial promotion remain open.
